premise: I spent my entire $110,000 divorce settlement to buy into my son’s organic mushroom farm, securing a signed partnership agreement for 49% of the business; once he landed a $1.3 million contract with a national grocery chain, he filed an amendment I’d supposedly signed giving me only a flat $10,000 buyout and barred me from the farm. I proved the amendment was a forgery, and the court voided it, awarding me full ownership because he’d diverted partnership funds to personal accounts — now I run ‘Morel of the Story Mushrooms,’ I supply the same chain with co-branded products, and my son works as my field hand wearing a shirt that says ‘My Spores Are Real.’
